jobs.title: Sr. Developer Advocate, AI and Machine Learning
Sr. Developer Advocate, AI and Machine Learning

reading.body:
Two AI developer-relations openings appear in this data, both Databricks, both the same senior title, posted the same day in Seattle and San Francisco.

The pattern is one employer staffing a single role across two locations, not a broad market for the function. Identical titles and identical posting dates point to one requisition replicated per site, which is how large companies fill a team across multiple offices. Developer relations and education is a customer-facing and community-facing function, so it sits downstream of a product that already exists rather than of new compute.

For AI specifically, this says little about capacity. The roles are about teaching and supporting developers who use machine learning tools, not about building data centers, securing power, or operating clusters. Nothing here measures how much compute Databricks runs or where it runs it.

What it does not tell the reader: two postings is a thin sample, and the count reflects only what the listed sources captured on one build date. Aggregators and company career boards differ in coverage, so the absence of other employers in this function is not evidence of absent demand. The data records postings, not hires, and carries no salary, no team size, and no indication of whether either role was filled.
